marble.name: Separating Mixtures
marble.subject: Science
marble.description: Use knowledge of solids, liquids, and gases to decide how mixtures might be separated through filtering, sieving, and evaporating
marble.prompt: If you has a mixture of sand, salt, and water, can they figure out a step-by-step plan to separate all three using a sieve, filter, and evaporation?

cluster.summary: Your child is exploring the materials around them — identifying different substances like wood, plastic, and metal, and discovering their properties such as whether they're hard or soft, rough or smooth.

misconceptions: Filtering can separate a dissolved solid from its solution (it passes straight through).
Sieving and filtering are the same technique.
Evaporating destroys the dissolved solid rather than leaving it behind.
Any mixture can be separated by a single step, ignoring the need for a sequence.
The order of steps does not matter.
representations: A separation planner routing a mixture through sieve/filter/evaporate/magnet stations
Property tags on each component (soluble / insoluble / magnetic / grain-size)
The canonical sand+salt+water sequence (filter then evaporate)
Apparatus diagrams (filter funnel, evaporating dish) linked to what each separates
authoredAnswer: Filter FIRST: the sand stays on the filter paper (insoluble), the salt-water solution passes through into the beaker. Rinse/dry the sand. Then EVAPORATE the filtered solution so the water leaves and dry salt is recovered. The critical move is filtering before evaporating — the child must exploit that sand is insoluble and salt is dissolved.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: heats the whole mixture first, ending with salt caked into the sand — cannot then separate them
wrongAnswers.fix: Don't just correct the order — ask 'which of these is dissolved and which is just floating?'; rebuild from the property (insoluble vs dissolved), then let them re-plan.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: surprised the filtrate is salty; treats filtering as removing all solids including dissolved ones
wrongAnswers.fix: Taste/evaporate a drop of the filtrate to show salt passed through — filters catch undissolved bits, not dissolved substances. Reconnect to what dissolving means.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: can recite 'filter then evaporate' for THIS setup but picks wrongly when the mixture changes (e.g. iron filings + sand)
wrongAnswers.fix: Don't reteach the concept — prompt 'what's different about these two substances that we can use?' so the choice is driven by properties (magnetism, solubility, particle size), not by recall.
